seeds.sentence: The three stages are attention page, first tip, and supporter loop.
Reply to every first-time supporter and every tip above your median tier.
Everything in lesson three said remove friction.
Edge case: at scale you cannot reply to everyone.
Every mechanic we build in this course is derived from that one principle.
Conversion happens once and the loop never forms.
Lesson three, the tipping widget itself.
Identity has to be the first screen, because every downstream concept, the attention page, the first tip, the supporter loop, is derived from the badge being real.
A tip without one is a transaction.
The supporter loop is the cycle where a first tip leads to a thank you, the thank you leads to a reply, and the reply leads to a second tip.
The loop is the moat, and it is derived from every principle in this course, trust before ask, verified identity, and friction where friction belongs.
If the supporter cannot tell a human from a bot farm, the first tip never happens.
The edge case: custom amounts still matter, but only above the top tier.
The mechanic nobody teaches: thank supporters within twenty four hours, personally, by name.
The widget is the part of the attention page where money actually moves, and the mechanic that matters most is tip tiers.
Build the message field first, and never charge extra for it, because the moment it costs money nobody writes one.
So the first lesson is simple.
Before any tips exist, you need verified identity, because verified identity is the prerequisite for everything the trust funnel does later.
The first tip is where a follower becomes a supporter with a small amount of money.
A sales funnel drives toward a transaction.
The supporter loop is where a supporter comes back, and that loop is where almost all of the revenue actually lives.
Here is the edge case almost everyone misses: if your page asks for money before it earns trust, every downstream metric looks fine until it suddenly does not.
So tiers convert better than a blank custom field, and this is not ideology, it is measured across every tipping platform that publishes numbers.
Tip with message looks like a small feature but it is the seed of the supporter loop we cover next lesson.
Anonymous pages convert at launch and die within a month, because the trust never compounds.
So the rule is tiers for the median supporter, open field for the generous ones.
And friction in a thank you is exactly what you want.
The trust funnel is a sequence where every step exists only to earn the right to the next step.
The trust funnel drives toward a decision the supporter feels good about, which is why it converts better over time.
The attention page is where a stranger decides whether you are real.
What this changes about how you build: do not bolt verification on later as a feature flag.
A tip tier is a named preset amount with its own identity, like a three dollar espresso or a ten dollar latte.
Fixed tiers exist because choosing an amount is work, and work kills conversion.
The receipt is part of the transaction; the thank you is part of the relationship, and those are different artifacts that should never be the same email.
Verified identity contrasts with anonymous tipping pages, the kind where anyone can spin up a page in thirty seconds.
Verification adds friction, and friction at signup costs you roughly twenty percent of creators who would otherwise finish onboarding.
What this changes about how you decide: when you have to choose between a feature that speeds up payment and a feature that deepens the loop, choose the loop.
The loop does not require total coverage, it requires that the supporter believes coverage exists.
